#### Sevoflurane:

+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CMRO~2~ vs MAC | - Dose-dependent reduction in electrophysiological function (60% of total)                                                                            |
|                | - No effect on basal function (40% of total) – only reduced by hypothermia                                                                            |
|                |                                                                                                                                                       |
|                | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image001.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral oxygen consumption against isoflurane concentration"}                         |
|                |                                                                                                                                                       |
|                | - *Exponential decay → greater effect at low dose*                                                                                                    |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CBF vs CMRO~2~ | - Dose-dependent vasodilatation (↓L-Ca^2+^ activity, ↑NO activity)                                                                                    |
|                | - Coupling of CBF and CMRO~2~ impaired (not ablated)                                                                                                  |
|                |                                                                                                                                                       |
|                | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image002.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral blood flow against oxygen consumption at increasing volatile concentrations"} |
|                |                                                                                                                                                       |
|                | - *Slope* ∝ *dose → greater effect at high dose*                                                                                                      |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CBF vs MAC\*   | - At low concentration: indirect vasoconstriction (via ↓CMRO~2~) wins                                                                                 |
|                | - At high concentration: direct vasodilatation wins                                                                                                   |
|                |                                                                                                                                                       |
|                | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image003.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral blood flow against isoflurane concentration"}                                 |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Other          | - Luxury perfusion: due to ↓CMRO~2~ but ↑CBF                                                                                                          |
|                | - Hypoventilation: ↑PaCO~2~ may cause further vasodilatation (if spont vent)                                                                          |
+----------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Propofol:

+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CMRO2 vs Ce  | - Same as for sevoflurane                                                                                                     |
|              |                                                                                                                               |
|              | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image004.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral oxygen consumption against propofol concentration"}   |
+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CMRO2 vs CBF | - Coupling of CBF and CMRO~2~ unaffected                                                                                      |
|              |                                                                                                                               |
|              | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image005.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral blood flow against oxygen consumption with propofol"} |
+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CBF vs Ce    | - Dose-dependent ↓CBF (ideal agent in intracranial hypertension)                                                              |
|              | - Note exponential decay                                                                                                      |
|              |                                                                                                                               |
|              | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image006.jpg){fig-alt="Cerebral blood flow against propofol concentration"}           |
+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Other        | - ↑↑Propofol Ce → ↓SVR → ↓mAP → ↓perfusion                                                                                    |
|              |   - Autoregulation exhausted if mAP \<50mmHg                                                                                  |
+--------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### \*Addendum

- This graph is from Miller’s Anesthesia, Chapter 11
- The data are from Anesthesiology (<https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3740503/>)
- At 0.5 MAC, mean values for local blood flow were reduced in every grey matter tissue
- However, none of the individual changes was statistically significant due to a large standard deviation
- My personal opinion is:
  - It is unlikely that a universal decrement in mean blood flow between 0 MAC and 0.5 MAC was due to chance
  - Statistical significance would have been reached had sample sizes been larger
  - These findings are consistent with the curves for CBF vs CMRO~2~ and CMRO~2~ vs MAC
- The alternative opinion is:
  - There is no evidence for significant change in CBF between 0 MAC and 1 MAC
  - In this range, the indirect vasoconstriction (via ↓CMRO~2~) and the direct vasodilation roughly cancel each other out
  - This is consistent with the leftward/upward shift in the CBF vs mAP curve that occurs with any concentration of volatile anaesthetic
  - See the Eger-Stoelting version below:

![](/content/exams/anzca/2021/A/2/prize-image007.png){fig-alt="Cerebral blood flow against MAC for halothane, enflurane and isoflurane with standard errors"}
